subject: P2_AC
topic: International Economic Institutions (WTO, IMF, World Bank, UNCTAD)

questions.q: The Bretton Woods Conference held in July 1944 led to the establishment of which twin international institutions?
opts: International Monetary Fund (IMF) and International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)
World Trade Organization (WTO) and United Nations (UN)
Asian Development Bank (ADB) and New Development Bank (NDB)
Bank for International Settlements (BIS) and OECD
questions.exp: The United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire (1944) created the 'Bretton Woods Twins': the IMF and the World Bank (IBRD).

questions.q: The headquarters of both the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank are located in:
questions.exp: Both the IMF and the World Bank Group have their global headquarters in Washington, D.C., United States.

questions.q: Which institution in the World Bank Group is known as the 'Soft Loan Window' because it provides interest-free loans (credits) and grants to the poorest developing countries?
opts: International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID)
questions.exp: The International Development Association (IDA), established in 1960, provides concessional interest-free loans ('credits') with long maturities to low-income nations.

questions.q: Which member of the World Bank Group specifically provides equity financing, long-term commercial loans, and advisory services directly to private sector enterprises in developing countries?
opts: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)
questions.exp: The IFC (established in 1956) is the private sector arm of the World Bank Group, investing directly in private sector companies in emerging markets without government guarantees.

questions.q: The Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA), a member of the World Bank Group, was established in 1988 primarily to:
opts: Promote foreign direct investment into developing countries by providing political risk insurance (guarantees) against non-commercial risks
Provide emergency short-term liquidity during balance of payment crises
Arbitrate bilateral investment disputes between private corporations
Regulate global maritime shipping freight rates
questions.exp: MIGA promotes foreign direct investment (FDI) into developing nations by insuring cross-border investors and lenders against non-commercial / political risks (expropriation, war, transfer restrictions, breach of contract).

questions.q: Which institution in the World Bank Group provides international facilities for conciliation and arbitration of investment disputes between foreign investors and sovereign states?
opts: ICSID (International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes)
questions.exp: ICSID, established in 1966 under the Washington Convention, is the premier institution for resolving legal disputes between international investors and host states.

questions.q: India is a member of all World Bank Group institutions EXCEPT:
questions.exp: India is a founding member of IBRD, IDA, IFC, and joined MIGA in 1994, but India is NOT a member of ICSID (International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes).

questions.q: The World Trade Organization (WTO) officially commenced operations on:
questions.exp: The WTO came into operation on January 1, 1995, following the signing of the Marrakesh Agreement on April 15, 1994, replacing GATT.

questions.q: The World Trade Organization (WTO) was established as a result of negotiations conducted during the:
questions.exp: The 8th GATT round of multilateral trade negotiations, the Uruguay Round (1986-1994), culminated in the Marrakesh Declaration and the creation of the WTO.

questions.q: Where is the headquarters of the World Trade Organization (WTO) located?
questions.exp: The headquarters of the WTO is situated at the Centre William Rappard in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.q: The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) was signed in 1947 and entered into force in:
questions.exp: GATT was signed by 23 nations in Geneva in October 1947 and took effect on January 1, 1948, as an interim agreement pending the creation of the ITO.

questions.q: The proposed international institution from the 1944 Bretton Woods architecture that failed to be ratified by the US Senate and was subsequently replaced by GATT was the:
questions.exp: The Havana Charter (1948) proposed the creation of the International Trade Organization (ITO), but failed ratification in the US Congress, leaving GATT as the primary trade framework until 1995.

questions.q: What are the two foundational non-discrimination principles of the WTO / GATT system?
opts: Most-Favoured-Nation (MFN) Principle and National Treatment Principle
Free Trade Principle and Fair Wage Principle
Absolute Cost Principle and Comparative Advantage Principle
questions.exp: The non-discrimination pillar of the WTO rests on two rules: MFN (treating foreign trade partners equally without discrimination) and National Treatment (treating foreign and domestic goods/services equally once imported).

questions.q: Under the Most-Favoured-Nation (MFN) principle (GATT Article I), a trade concession granted by one WTO member to another member must be:
opts: Extended immediately and unconditionally to all other WTO member countries
Restricted only to bilateral allies sharing the same continent
Charged an extra transit fee by third-party nations
Approved by a unanimous vote of the United Nations General Assembly
questions.exp: The MFN principle requires that any advantage, favor, or privilege granted to products originating in or destined for any country must be accorded unconditionally to all other contracting parties.

questions.q: The National Treatment Principle (GATT Article III) mandates that:
opts: Imported goods, once they have cleared customs, must be treated no less favorably than domestically produced goods in terms of internal taxes and regulations
All national industries must be state-owned
Foreign firms must pay double the domestic corporate tax rate
Domestic citizens must be prioritized over foreign goods during shortages
questions.exp: National Treatment prohibits internal taxes, domestic charges, or administrative regulations that discriminate against foreign imported goods after customs clearance.

questions.q: Which WTO agreement deals with standards, availability, and enforcement of Intellectual Property Rights?
opts: TRIPS (Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights)
GATS (General Agreement on Trade in Services)
questions.exp: The TRIPS Agreement sets minimum global standards for the protection and enforcement of patents, copyrights, trademarks, industrial designs, geographical indications, and trade secrets.

questions.q: Under the TRIPS agreement of the WTO, what is the standard minimum protection period mandated for Patents?
opts: 50 years after the death of the inventor
Indefinite period subject to annual registration
questions.exp: Article 33 of TRIPS mandates that the term of protection available for patents shall not end before the expiration of a period of 20 years counted from the filing date.

questions.q: Under TRIPS, the protection term for Copyrights (literary, artistic, and musical works) generally lasts for:
opts: The life of the author plus at least 50 years after their death
20 years from the date of publication
questions.exp: Under TRIPS and the Berne Convention, copyright protection covers the author's lifespan plus a minimum of 50 years after death.

questions.q: The Agreement on Trade-Related Investment Measures (TRIMS) under the WTO prohibits investment measures that violate:
opts: National Treatment (GATT Art. III) and General Elimination of Quantitative Restrictions (GATT Art. XI)
questions.exp: TRIMS prohibits investment requirements that restrict trade or discriminate against foreign investors, such as Local Content Requirements (LCRs) and Trade Balancing Requirements.

questions.q: Which of the following investment measures is explicitly prohibited under the WTO TRIMS agreement?
opts: Mandating foreign firms to use a specified proportion of locally sourced inputs (Local Content Requirement)
Requiring foreign firms to comply with national safety standards
Levying uniform corporate income taxes on foreign enterprises
questions.exp: Local Content Requirements (LCRs) and export-import balancing rules are trade-distorting and violate TRIMS.

questions.q: The General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS) classifies international service delivery into how many distinct 'Modes of Supply'?
questions.exp: GATS categorizes trade in services into 4 modes: Cross-border supply (Mode 1), Consumption abroad (Mode 2), Commercial presence (Mode 3), and Presence of natural persons (Mode 4).

questions.q:
Match the GATS Modes of Supply with their correct definitions:
(a) Mode 1 - (i) Consumption Abroad (e.g., medical tourism, international students)
(b) Mode 2 - (ii) Cross-Border Supply (e.g., software/BPO services over the internet)
(c) Mode 3 - (iii) Commercial Presence (e.g., establishing a foreign bank branch)
(d) Mode 4 - (iv) Presence of Natural Persons (e.g., software consultants traveling abroad)
questions.exp: Mode 1: Cross-border supply; Mode 2: Consumption abroad; Mode 3: Commercial presence (FDI); Mode 4: Movement of natural persons.

questions.q: Under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture (AoA), which 'Box' contains agricultural subsidies that are considered trade-distorting and are subject to reduction commitments?
questions.exp: Amber Box covers all domestic agricultural support measures that distort international trade and production (e.g., price supports like MSP, input subsidies), subject to reduction commitments.

questions.q: Under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, subsidies in the 'Green Box' are:
opts: Permitted without limit because they cause minimal or no trade-distorting effects (e.g., R&D, pest control, food security stocks, environmental programs)
Subject to mandatory annual 20% tariff increases
Restricted only to African developing nations
questions.exp: Green Box subsidies (direct income support, R&D, infrastructure, disaster relief) are non-trade-distorting and exempt from reduction commitments.

questions.q: Under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, 'Blue Box' subsidies refer to:
opts: Amber box subsidies with conditions designed to reduce distortion by placing direct production-limiting requirements on farmers
Illegal subsidies subject to immediate international trade embargoes
Subsidies on ocean fisheries and maritime transport
Subsidies given exclusively for space research
questions.exp: The Blue Box covers Amber Box supports tied to direct payments under production-limiting programs, exempt from reduction commitments.

questions.q: The 'De Minimis' support level allowed for trade-distorting agricultural subsidies (Amber Box) under the WTO AoA is:
opts: 5% of total value of agricultural output for developed countries and 10% for developing countries
20% for developed countries and 5% for developing countries
questions.exp: De Minimis thresholds allow Amber Box support up to 5% of agricultural production value for developed countries and up to 10% for developing countries.

questions.q: The 'Peace Clause' negotiated at the WTO Bali Ministerial Conference (2013) protects developing countries like India from legal disputes regarding:
opts: Public stockholding programs for food security purposes exceeding Amber Box subsidy limits
Exporting textile garments below factory cost
Imposing higher custom duties on digital downloads
questions.exp: The Bali Peace Clause provides interim immunity to developing countries against challenges under the AoA for breaching agricultural subsidy limits during public food stockholding for domestic food security.

questions.q: What is the highest decision-making body of the World Trade Organization (WTO)?
opts: The Ministerial Conference (meeting at least once every two years)
questions.exp: The Ministerial Conference, composed of trade ministers from all member countries, is the supreme governing body of the WTO, meeting at least once every two years.

questions.q: When the WTO Ministerial Conference is not in session, its day-to-day functions are carried out by the:
opts: General Council (which also convenes as the Dispute Settlement Body and Trade Policy Review Body)
questions.exp: The General Council, based in Geneva, conducts WTO operations between Ministerial Conferences and convenes as both the DSB and the TPRB.

questions.q: Decisions in the World Trade Organization (WTO) are generally made on the basis of:
opts: Consensus among all member nations (one member, one vote)
Weighted voting based on financial capital quotas
Veto power reserved for the G-7 industrialized nations
questions.exp: Unlike the IMF/World Bank, the WTO operates primarily on consensus, with each member country holding one vote under formal procedures.

questions.q: Under the WTO Dispute Settlement Mechanism, if a panel report is appealed, it is heard by the:
opts: International Court of Justice at The Hague
Secretary General of the United Nations
questions.exp: The WTO Appellate Body, established in 1995, consists of 7 rotating judges appointed for 4-year terms to review legal points in panel reports.

questions.q: The United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) was established in:
questions.exp: UNCTAD was established in 1964 as a permanent intergovernmental body of the UN General Assembly, headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.q: Who was the renowned Argentine economist and structuralist who served as the first Secretary-General of UNCTAD?
questions.exp: Raúl Prebisch, co-author of the Prebisch-Singer thesis on the deteriorating terms of trade for primary commodity exporters, served as UNCTAD's first Secretary-General (1964-1969).

questions.q: The Prebisch-Singer Thesis argues that over the long term, developing countries face:
opts: Deteriorating Terms of Trade because prices of primary commodity exports fall relative to prices of manufactured imports
Higher productivity growth than industrialized nations
questions.exp: The Prebisch-Singer thesis posits that the net barter terms of trade secularly deteriorate for primary commodity-exporting developing nations relative to manufactured goods-exporting developed countries.

questions.q: The Generalized System of Preferences (GSP), which allows developed countries to extend lower or zero tariff rates to goods from developing nations on a non-reciprocal basis, was instituted through:
opts: UNCTAD (at UNCTAD II in New Delhi, 1968)
questions.exp: The GSP framework was adopted in 1968 at UNCTAD II held in New Delhi, granting non-reciprocal tariff preferences to developing country exports.

questions.q: Which annual flagship report is published by UNCTAD to track global trends in Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)?
questions.exp: UNCTAD publishes the annual 'World Investment Report', analyzing global and regional trends in foreign direct investment (FDI).

questions.q: The 'World Development Report' (WDR) is the annual flagship publication of:
questions.exp: The World Development Report (WDR) is published annually by the World Bank since 1978, focusing on key economic and social development topics.

questions.q: The 'World Economic Outlook' (WEO) and the 'Global Financial Stability Report' (GFSR) are published semiannually by:
questions.exp: The IMF publishes both the World Economic Outlook (WEO) and the Global Financial Stability Report (GFSR) twice a year.

questions.q: What is the primary function of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)?
opts: To oversee international monetary stability, promote exchange rate stability, and provide short-to-medium-term balance of payments financing to member nations
To fund long-term education and health projects in low-income nations
To enforce patent registrations for pharmaceutical MNCs
To act as the global commercial lender of first resort
questions.exp: The primary role of the IMF is macroeconomic surveillance, promoting exchange stability, fostering global trade, and providing balance of payments financial assistance.

questions.q: The voting power and borrowing capacity of a member country in the IMF are determined primarily by its:
opts: IMF Quota Subscription (based on relative economic size, openness, variability, and reserves)
questions.exp: An IMF member's quota determines its financial contribution, voting weight, SDR allocation, and maximum borrowing capacity.

questions.q: Which IMF lending facility was created to provide financial assistance to member countries facing deep structural economic and balance of payments difficulties requiring medium-term macroeconomic reforms?
questions.exp: The Extended Fund Facility (EFF), established in 1974, provides medium-to-long term assistance (3-4 years) to overcome structural balance of payments weaknesses.

questions.q: The Poverty Reduction and Growth Facility (PRGF), now superseded by the Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust (PRGT) in the IMF, provides:
opts: Concessional (zero-interest or low-interest) financial assistance to low-income developing nations
High-interest commercial loans to Fortune 500 companies
Equity investments in European stock markets
Funding for private speculative venture capital funds
questions.exp: The PRGT provides concessional, low- or zero-interest financing to support low-income countries in achieving sustainable balance of payments and poverty reduction.

questions.q: What is 'IMF Conditionality'?
opts: Policy requirements and structural reform benchmarks that a borrowing country must implement in exchange for accessing IMF financial assistance
A rule requiring borrowing countries to change their national currency name
A requirement for borrowing countries to surrender all domestic gold mines to the IMF
Mandatory transfer of domestic central bank ownership to Washington
questions.exp: IMF Conditionality refers to macroeconomic policy adjustments, fiscal targets, and structural reforms that borrowing nations agree to carry out to restore economic stability.

questions.q:
Chronologically arrange the following GATT/WTO trade negotiation rounds:
(A) Kennedy Round
(B) Geneva Round (Founding GATT)
(C) Uruguay Round
(D) Tokyo Round
questions.exp: Order: 1. Geneva Round (1947) -> 2. Kennedy Round (1964-1967) -> 3. Tokyo Round (1973-1979) -> 4. Uruguay Round (1986-1994).

questions.q:
Match the WTO Ministerial Conferences with the correct Host Cities and Years:
(a) 1st Ministerial Conference - (i) Singapore (1996)
(b) 4th Ministerial Conference - (ii) Doha, Qatar (2001)
(c) 9th Ministerial Conference - (iii) Bali, Indonesia (2013)
(d) 11th Ministerial Conference - (iv) Buenos Aires, Argentina (2017)
questions.exp: 1st: Singapore (1996); 4th: Doha (2001 - launch of Doha Development Agenda); 9th: Bali (2013 - Bali Package/TFA); 11th: Buenos Aires (2017).

questions.q:
The 'Singapore Issues' introduced at the 1996 WTO Singapore Ministerial Conference comprised which four subjects?
(i) Investment
(ii) Competition Policy
(iii) Transparency in Government Procurement
(iv) Trade Facilitation
(v) Agricultural Subsidies
questions.exp: The four Singapore Issues were: Investment, Competition Policy, Transparency in Government Procurement, and Trade Facilitation.

questions.q: The Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA), which entered into force in February 2017 following the Bali Package, aims to:
opts: Speed up the movement, release, and clearance of cross-border goods through modern, transparent customs procedures
Ban all import tariffs globally by 2030
Abolish national patents for clean tech
questions.exp: The TFA contains provisions for expediting goods movement, release, and clearance, including goods in transit, by modernizing customs infrastructure.

questions.q: Which WTO agreement establishes rules and disciplines for government purchases of goods and services above specified monetary thresholds?
opts: Agreement on Subsidies and Countervailing Measures (ASCM)
questions.exp: The Agreement on Government Procurement (GPA) is a plurilateral agreement within the WTO framework that applies only to signatories that choose to join it.

questions.q: A 'Plurilateral Agreement' in the WTO framework is an agreement that:
opts: Binds only those WTO members that explicitly choose to sign and ratify it, rather than all WTO members automatically
Binds every single member of the WTO universally through a single undertaking
Applies only to sovereign states with nuclear technology
questions.exp: Unlike multilateral WTO agreements under the 'single undertaking' rule, plurilateral agreements (e.g., GPA, Civil Aircraft) apply only to members that voluntarily sign them.

questions.q: Under the WTO Agreement on Subsidies and Countervailing Measures (ASCM), subsidies are classified into:
opts: Prohibited Subsidies (Red Box), Actionable Subsidies (Amber Box), and Non-actionable Subsidies (Green Box - expired)
Domestic Subsidies, Export Taxes, and Import Surcharges
Direct Taxes, Indirect Taxes, and Surcharges
questions.exp: ASCM establishes two main categories: Prohibited subsidies (contingent on export performance or local content use) and Actionable subsidies (actionable if causing adverse trade effects).

questions.q: Under the WTO ASCM, 'Prohibited Subsidies' include subsidies that are contingent upon:
opts: Export performance or the use of domestic over imported goods (local content)
Disaster relief compensation to natural calamity victims
questions.exp: Export-contingent subsidies and local content-contingent subsidies are red-light / prohibited subsidies under ASCM.

questions.q: Which WTO body conducts periodic surveillance of the national trade policies and practices of member countries to enhance transparency?
questions.exp: The Trade Policy Review Mechanism (TPRM), conducted by the TPRB, regularly evaluates member trade regimes to ensure transparency and compliance.

questions.q: In the WTO Dispute Settlement Body, what is the 'Reverse Consensus' (Negative Consensus) rule?
opts: A panel report or appellate decision is automatically adopted UNLESS every single member country present votes against its adoption
A dispute can proceed only if all members vote in favor unanimously
The losing country can unilaterally veto the final panel report
Only the WTO Director-General has the vote
questions.exp: Under the reverse consensus rule, panel formation, report adoption, and retaliation authorization occur automatically unless there is a unanimous consensus against them.

questions.q: Geographical Indications (GIs) protected under the WTO TRIPS agreement identify a product as originating from a specific territory where its:
opts: Quality, reputation, or other characteristic is essentially attributable to its geographical origin (e.g., Darjeeling Tea, Champagne, Basmati)
Manufacturing company is owned by the state
questions.exp: A Geographical Indication (GI) identifies a good as originating in a specific locality where a given quality, reputation, or characteristic is essentially attributable to its geographic origin.

questions.q: Which international convention signed in 1883 laid the foundation for the international protection of Industrial Property (Patents, Trademarks, Industrial Designs)?
opts: Paris Convention for the Protection of Industrial Property (1883)
Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works (1886)
questions.exp: The Paris Convention (1883) was the first major international treaty protecting industrial intellectual property rights (patents, designs, trademarks).

questions.q: The Berne Convention of 1886 deals with the international protection of:
questions.exp: The Berne Convention (1886) governs the international protection of copyright for literary, dramatic, musical, and artistic works.

questions.q: The 'Patent Cooperation Treaty' (PCT), administered by WIPO (World Intellectual Property Organization), allows inventors to:
opts: Seek patent protection for an invention simultaneously in a large number of member countries by filing a single 'international' patent application
Get a universal patent that automatically grants protection in all UN countries with zero national examination
Circumvent payment of any national renewal fees permanently
Transfer patent ownership automatically to the United Nations
questions.exp: The PCT (1970) streamlines the initial filing process, enabling an applicant to file one international application to reserve patent priority across member nations.

questions.q: The Madrid System (Madrid Agreement and Madrid Protocol) provides a cost-effective mechanism for the international registration of:
questions.exp: The Madrid System, administered by WIPO, provides a centralized system for registering and managing trademarks internationally across multiple jurisdictions.

questions.q: The Special Drawing Right (SDR) is an interest-bearing international reserve asset created by the IMF. How is the value of 1 SDR determined?
opts: By a weighted basket of five major currencies (US Dollar, Euro, Chinese Renminbi, Japanese Yen, British Pound)
By the market spot price of 1 ounce of pure gold in London
By the average price of crude oil per barrel
By the consumer price index of the United States
questions.exp: The value of the SDR is calculated daily based on market exchange rates of a fixed basket of five major currencies: USD, EUR, CNY, JPY, and GBP.

questions.q: In which year did the IMF officially include the Chinese Renminbi (Yuan) into the SDR currency valuation basket?
questions.exp: The IMF Executive Board decided in November 2015 to include the Chinese Renminbi (CNY) into the SDR basket, effective October 1, 2016.

questions.q: The IMF loan facility designed to provide rapid, low-access, emergency financial assistance to member countries without traditional ex-post conditionality during natural disasters or health crises is the:
opts: Rapid Financing Instrument (RFI) / Rapid Credit Facility (RCF)
questions.exp: The RFI provides rapid, low-access emergency financial support to countries facing urgent balance of payments needs without full program conditionality.

questions.q: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS), which formulates international regulatory capital standards for commercial banks (Basel I, II, III), is housed at the:
opts: Bank for International Settlements (BIS) in Basel, Switzerland
questions.exp: The BCBS is hosted and supported by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), headquartered in Basel, Switzerland.

questions.q: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS), founded in 1930, is often described as the:
opts: Development Bank of the United Nations
questions.exp: The BIS is the world's oldest international financial institution and acts as a specialized bank and forum for national central banks.

questions.q: The Doha Development Agenda (DDA) launched at the 4th WTO Ministerial Conference in 2001 focused primarily on:
opts: Improving trade prospects and market access for developing nations, especially in agriculture and non-agricultural market access (NAMA)
Abolishing the United Nations Security Council
Banning export of all pharmaceutical medicines
questions.exp: The Doha Round aimed to place developing nations' needs and integration (market access in agriculture, development flexibilities, special and differential treatment) at the center of WTO negotiations.

questions.q: What is 'Special and Differential Treatment' (S&DT) under WTO provisions?
opts: Special rights, longer transition periods, and lower commitment thresholds granted to developing and least-developed country members
Exclusive trade privileges granted only to the United States and the European Union
Higher customs duties permitted only on military exports
An exemption allowing developed countries to ignore all environmental norms
questions.exp: S&DT provisions give developing and least-developed countries special rights, including longer implementation periods, technical assistance, and lower reduction commitments.

questions.q: Compulsory Licensing under the WTO TRIPS Agreement allows a sovereign government to:
opts: Authorize the domestic production or importation of a patented pharmaceutical drug without the consent of the patent owner during public health emergencies
Steal patents from foreign firms for commercial resale
Cancel all patent rights across every domestic industry permanently
Force foreign doctors to practice in government hospitals
questions.exp: Under TRIPS Article 31 and the 2001 Doha Declaration on TRIPS and Public Health, governments can issue compulsory licenses to produce affordable generic medicines during public health crises.

questions.q: The 'Nairobi Package' agreed upon at the 10th WTO Ministerial Conference (2015) included a historic milestone agreement regarding:
opts: The complete elimination of agricultural export subsidies by member nations
The introduction of a global carbon tax
The complete privatization of all national postal services
The banning of cross-border container shipping
questions.exp: The 2015 Nairobi Ministerial Conference adopted a landmark decision committing developed and developing members to eliminate agricultural export subsidies.

questions.q:
Match the following World Bank Group Institutions with their year of establishment:
(a) IBRD - (i) 1944
(b) IFC - (ii) 1956
(c) IDA - (iii) 1960
(d) MIGA - (iv) 1988
questions.exp: IBRD was founded in 1944; IFC in 1956; IDA in 1960; MIGA in 1988 (and ICSID in 1966).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an institution of the World Bank Group?
questions.exp: The IMF is a separate Bretton Woods institution, not an agency of the World Bank Group. The World Bank Group consists of IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA, and ICSID.

questions.q: In the WTO TRIPS framework, what is a 'Patent'?
opts: An exclusive right granted for an invention (a product or process providing a new way of doing something or offering a new technical solution)
A distinctive sign identifying certain goods or services produced by an individual or enterprise
A legal term describing rights granted to creators for their literary and artistic works
A trade secret regarding internal employee compensation
questions.exp: A patent is an exclusive legal right granted for a novel, inventive, and industrially applicable product or process for a specified period (20 years).

questions.q: A 'Trademark' under intellectual property law protects:
opts: Distinctive signs, symbols, logos, words, or slogans used to distinguish goods or services of one enterprise from those of others
Literary books and computer programming source codes
questions.exp: Trademarks protect distinctive brand identifiers (names, logos, symbols) that differentiate goods/services in the marketplace.

questions.q: The Trade and Development Report (TDR) is an annual publication produced by:
questions.exp: UNCTAD publishes the Trade and Development Report (TDR) annually, analyzing global macroeconomic trends and developmental policies.
